adjudicatedExecutionSummary.method: Complete matrix under current revision 4; no overrides or criterion changes.

findings.criterion: A06 modal Escape and focus restoration
findings.title: WebKit pointer-opened task dialog does not return focus to its invoker
findings.impact: After opening New task with a pointer and dismissing with Escape, focus stays on BODY instead of New task. Subsequent keyboard navigation restarts from the page rather than the invoking control.
refutationChecks: The dialog actually closes; the remaining failure is focus restoration.
Focus is still BODY after 550 ms, ruling out an asynchronous close-event observation.
Genuine keyboard opening restores focus correctly; the issue is not generalized to all keyboard use.
Chromium passes both pointer and keyboard paths.
run-08 passes all eight identical probes; the result is not a browser-wide inability to restore focus.
Positive and deliberately focus-losing fixtures validate the A06 observer.
sourceEvidence: artifact/app.js:263 stores document.activeElement, which is BODY after WebKit pointer activation.
artifact/app.js:273 focuses that connected BODY rather than the invocation button.

exploratoryFindings.contractAmbiguity: The brief reserves the select value all for the All projects sentinel while allowing any nonempty project string, including all. This edge was not in the predeclared concrete fixtures; selecting the distinct project option should still be distinguishable from selecting the sentinel.
exploratoryFindings.impact: No collision observed: the distinct project option isolates the intended record, and storage remains unchanged.
repro: In an isolated context load the same valid two-task board used for all four apps: project all and project Atlas.
Select the actual project option labelled all. A capture-phase event trace confirms selectedIndex 1 before and after candidate handlers.
Compare rendered task IDs and saved bytes.
sourceEvidence: artifact/app.js:177 restores the project by selectedIndex while retaining a separate projectAll flag.
artifact/app.js:216 distinguishes the All projects flag from the literal project name all.

adjudication.scopeLimit: The primary score covers 16 predefined contract groups. Exploratory edge findings are reported separately and do not alter that score. Neither is a universal security/accessibility/design certification.

adjudication-focus/results.json.criterion: A06 modal close and focus restoration
adjudication-focus/results.json.purpose: Refute action timing and compare pointer vs genuine keyboard opening before deciding whether the observed WebKit failure is a product issue.

exploratory-project-sentinel/selection-t.purpose: Refute incorrect selector or option ambiguity; diagnostic capture only, original fixture and primary scores unchanged.

designReview.method: Single qualitative review of actual captured desktop and mobile pixels. No numerical aesthetic score.

observations.observation: The desktop separates workspace and project navigation in a left rail, an introductory heading and New task action, a summary strip, and a clearly labelled Studio board with search and three status columns. Card titles are visually stronger than project names, tags, and dates.
observations.implication: Navigation, creation, overview, and individual work items have identifiable positions and a consistent reading order.

observations.observation: A cream and sage palette, dark green text, serif display headings, repeated thin borders, and small line icons are consistent across the board and side rail. Project labels, date text, tags, and secondary explanatory lines are considerably smaller and lighter than task titles.
observations.implication: The repeated visual treatment is coherent, and the title hierarchy supports scanning. Users must look more closely to read fine metadata or distinguish the small edit and delete icons; this is not a measured contrast or hit-area finding.

observations.observation: The form gives title and project explicit required labels, marks due date and tags optional, explains tag limits, and shows a strong focus outline on the title. The date field displays YYYY-MM-DD as a plain text entry without a visible calendar affordance. Create task is visually stronger than Cancel.
observations.implication: The required fields and save action are clear. Date entry depends on recognizing and typing the shown format, which is a usability tradeoff rather than evidence of invalid date handling.

observations.observation: The requested Research task appears with its title, High priority badge, evidence and launch tags, and date. Searching its title leaves that single card in the In progress column, shows a matching count and Clear filters, and labels the other columns No matching tasks in this column.
observations.implication: The task representation exposes the requested attributes. The search state explicitly distinguishes absent matches from a workspace with no tasks.

observations.observation: The malformed import state shows a prominent warm notice headed Import could not be completed, followed by This file is not valid JSON. Your prior board has not been replaced. A Dismiss control is visible and existing task cards remain on screen.
observations.implication: The notice explains the cause and preservation outcome in the same place. The capture receipt separately records unchanged stored bytes for this malformed input; the image alone does not establish complete import safety.

observations.observation: At 360 by 800, the sidebar becomes a compact top identity strip, the heading fits on one line, and the summary arranges three counts above a progress row. New task, search, and all three filters appear in the first viewport. The first task-column heading begins near the bottom, while task cards are below the captured viewport. No overlapping or clipped primary text is visible.
observations.implication: Creation and filtering are available before scrolling, but inspecting existing tasks still requires moving past the introduction and overview. A more compact overview could place actual work items closer to the initial viewport.

mobileLayoutObservation.note: The width values come from the capture receipt; they are not an aesthetic score. This observation covers the initial mobile viewport only.

limits: This review covers only the six supplied captured states. The mobile image is a first visit, not a complete mobile walkthrough.
Static pixels do not establish keyboard, screen-reader, motion, data-safety, or complete import correctness; those require the separate behavior rubric.
Board counts and progress belong to fictional seed data, not benchmark performance or adoption.
Partly visible surrounding content in anchored screenshots is capture framing, not proof that the source clips that content.
No condition mapping was inspected, no candidate source was edited, and no aesthetic score or causal improvement claim is made.
Visual appearance cannot reveal the generating agent planning, tool use, verification method, or experimental condition.

processReview.summary: The baseline app run expanded a passing suite, fixed modal Tab containment and finished with targeted responsive and stale-write checks.

observations.observed: The public outline separates board construction, storage recovery and cross-tab protection from browser workflow and responsive checks.
The candidate used the supplied browser and ran its main suite twice. It then expanded validation, imported-text, storage-denial and nested-path checks.
The edge suite failed when Tab left the modal. The candidate added explicit keyboard wrapping and reran the unchanged edge helper successfully.
After later edits, direct browser checks covered four viewport widths, reverse Tab wrapping, reduced-motion CSS and a stale-write guard. The trace shows no later full main-suite rerun.
The final record lists source, retained verification helpers, result files and captures, and states Chromium-only verification and session-only undo.

limits: The initially passing main suite did not cover the modal Tab-containment failure found by the added edge suite.
The saved main-suite result predates later tag-preservation and keyboard changes. Later edge and targeted checks passed, but a full final main-suite rerun is not recorded.
Candidate-authored checks are process evidence, not an independent acceptance result. No cross-engine, delegation or external orchestration was exercised.
This descriptive process audit was requested after outcomes existed. It is retrospective and exploratory, not a preregistered process endpoint.
The methods reviewer knows condition assignments; this review is not blinded. Separate proof/design reviewers have their own blinding procedures.
Only public progress messages, observable tool actions, check exits and retained artifact evidence are summarized. No hidden reasoning is inferred or published.
There is no process score, tool-call leaderboard or causal claim. More messages, calls, checks or elapsed time do not imply a better process.
The baseline retains native Codex instructions and the same common trial directions. It is not an unstructured or instruction-free model.
Delegation, external services and auxiliary model calls were prohibited for both conditions. Full orchestration, provider selection, collaboration and autonomous end-to-end deployment are unmeasured.
Treatment includes three or four pinned contracts plus a repository snapshot. Observed behavior cannot be assigned to an individual Fabius rule from this design.
Candidate-authored tests and self-reported passes are process evidence, not substitutes for the independent acceptance and proof checks.
Coverage includes all 12 finalized valid runs from the planned three-task, two-condition, two-repeat study. The two preserved setup attempts are documented separately.
